title: Is there an equilateral triangle for every side length?
description: The sides fifty, fifty and fifty are tested with the three steps, and then the same steps are used for any side length. The sum of the two equal sides is double the third, which is always more.
teaching_notes: One idea: for an equilateral triangle the other two sides add to double the longest, and a length is always less than its double. Watch for children who test only fifty and do not see why every side length works.

source: Does there exist an equilateral triangle with sides 50, 50, 50? In general, does there exist an equilateral triangle of any sidelength? Justify your answer.
video_script.why: The child knows how to build an equilateral triangle with two arcs and now sees why the check always passes.
video_script.substitution: The side length is fifty, and then any side length greater than zero.
video_script.anchor: Three equal sides of fifty, with the other two added together
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, an equilateral triangle exists for fifty, and for every side length.

final_answer.value: Yes: 50 < 50 + 50, and in general s < s + s for any side length s above zero
final_answer.spoken: yes, an equilateral triangle exists for fifty, and for every side length

never_show: the word yes before the answer beat
maths_rules: any side length s > 0: other two s + s = 2s; s < 2s, passes
check: arcs of radius 50 from both ends of a base of 50 meet above the base, the two-arcs construction
video_script.design: One idea: the other two sides add to double the longest, which is always more. The three equal sides stay in the anchor band; the working band holds the board solution.
